slides.title: Paper Information
bullets: Yao H, Zhang A, Li D, et al. BMJ 2024;384:e076410 (Open Access)
Design: systematic review and network meta-analysis
PROSPERO registration: CRD42022342845
Sources: PubMed, Web of Science, Cochrane CENTRAL, Embase (inception to 19 Aug 2023)

slides.title: Background
bullets: Diabetes: 476 million globally, 463 million with type 2 diabetes
GLP-1RAs: increase insulin secretion, inhibit glucagon, slow gastric emptying, reduce caloric intake and body weight
FDA approved: exenatide, liraglutide, dulaglutide, albiglutide, lixisenatide, semaglutide, tirzepatide
Novel drugs emerging: orforglipron, retatrutide, CagriSema — updated evidence synthesis urgently needed

slides.title: Objective
bullets: Evaluate comparative efficacy and safety of GLP-1RAs on glycaemic control, body weight, and lipid profile in adults with type 2 diabetes
Most complete GLP-1RA network to date: 15 drugs including latest novel agents pooled for the first time
Rank efficacy by SUCRA; explore dose-effect patterns

slides.title: Study Design
bullets: Eligibility: RCTs, adults 18-65 with type 2 diabetes, GLP-1RA vs placebo or GLP-1RA, follow-up >= 12 weeks
Excluded: crossover design, non-inferiority without placebo arm, withdrawn drugs, non-English
Three reviewers screened independently; fourth resolved conflicts
Risk of bias: Cochrane RoB 2.0; certainty: CINeMA framework

slides.title: Statistical Analysis
bullets: Frequentist network meta-analysis (Stata MVMETA), random effects, REML
Mean difference for continuous outcomes; odds ratio for adverse events (95% CI)
SUCRA curves ranked drug efficacy; node splitting checked consistency
Subgroups: dose, follow-up duration, single vs dual/triple agonists

slides.title: Study Characteristics
bullets: 16,316 citations -> 483 full text assessed -> 76 RCTs included
39,246 participants; 15 GLP-1RA drugs; 58 countries
Mean age 56.79 (SD 9.59); 54.06% men; diabetes duration 8.47 years
Baseline BMI 31.73; HbA1c 8.13%; intervention 12-78 weeks
Overall risk of bias: 13% of studies high risk

slides.title: Glycaemic Control
bullets: All 15 GLP-1RAs significantly lowered HbA1c vs placebo (56 trials, n=26,343)
Tirzepatide largest: -2.10% (95% CI -2.47 to -1.74), SUCRA 94.2%, high confidence
Fasting glucose: tirzepatide -3.12 mmol/L (-3.59 to -2.66), SUCRA 97.2%, high confidence

slides.title: HbA1c — Forest Plot (Fig 3)
slides.caption: Network effect sizes of 15 GLP-1RAs vs placebo for HbA1c (%); colours = CINeMA confidence

slides.title: Body Weight
bullets: 53 trials, 21,349 participants for body weight changes
CagriSema most effective: -14.03 kg (-17.05 to -11.00), high confidence
Tirzepatide -8.47 kg (-9.68 to -7.26); retatrutide -7.87 (-9.95 to -5.79)
Waist circumference: tirzepatide -6.77 cm; semaglutide -3.74 cm; liraglutide -2.30 cm

slides.title: Body Weight — Forest Plot (Fig 7)
slides.caption: Network effect sizes vs placebo for weight loss (kg); colours = CINeMA confidence

slides.title: Lipid Profile
bullets: Semaglutide: only GLP-1RA lowering LDL, -0.16 mmol/L (-0.30 to -0.02)
Semaglutide also lowered total cholesterol -0.48 (-0.84 to -0.11)
PEG-loxenatide: only drug raising HDL, 0.16 mmol/L (0.00 to 0.31)
Triglycerides: ITCA 650 -1.59; tirzepatide -0.89 mmol/L significant vs placebo

slides.title: Adverse Events
bullets: Discontinuation OR: lixisenatide 2.86 (1.48-5.51), semaglutide 2.61, exenatide 2.39, tirzepatide 2.30, liraglutide 2.15
Diarrhoea: CagriSema 6.60 (1.16-37.76); tirzepatide 2.88 (2.09-3.96)
Nausea elevated with 12 of 15 drugs; vomiting with 10 drugs
GI odds rose with increasing dose — warning for high dose administration

slides.title: Adverse Events (Fig 8)
slides.caption: Odds ratios vs placebo: discontinuation, diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting

slides.title: Principal Findings
bullets: Tirzepatide best for HbA1c and fasting glucose (high confidence of evidence)
CagriSema most effective for reducing body weight
Dual (tirzepatide, mazdutide, CagriSema) and triple (retatrutide) agonists outperform single agonists
Dose-dependent efficacy; tirzepatide 15 mg: discontinuation OR 2.26 (1.35 to 3.77)

slides.title: Limitations
bullets: Varied population characteristics and follow-up durations
Participants had little control over diet and exercise
Some trials lacked randomisation / blinding details
Some drugs involved few articles — interpret with caution
Open label design and pharmaceutical industry funding bias risk

slides.title: Take Home Message
bullets: GLP-1RAs much more effective than placebo in treating adults with type 2 diabetes
Tirzepatide: most effective on glycaemic control (HbA1c and fasting glucose)
CagriSema: best performance for weight loss
Safety concern: gastrointestinal adverse events, especially at high doses
